newsitem.title: UK: Avalon in bid to boost Orenburg oil output.
newsitem.headline: Avalon in bid to boost Orenburg oil output.

text.p: Britain's Avalon Oil Plc said on Wednesday it would buy a 30,000 barrels per day Early Production Facility from Halliburton Energy Services to boost output at the Orenburg field on Russia's southern border with Kazakhstan.

Avalon, a U.S.-based oil production and exploration company quoted on London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market, said the facility would boost output, when fully operational, to 10,000 bpd from 2,500 bpd.
"The new Early Production Facility will significantly enhance the exploitation of these resources," Avalon's chairman John Wieczorek said in a statement.
Current production had been hampered by the lack of above ground facilities.
No figures were given for how much the facility would cost.

The company also said Orenburggazprom -- a subsidiary of Russian gas giant RAO Gazprom GAZP.RTS -- had completed the transfer of $51 million worth of assets to Stimul, the joint venture 49 percent owned by Avalon.
Avalon said the assets comprised 51 wells located in the eastern end of the Orenburg field.

Stimul's most recent horizontal well, 29-2, has benefited from Avalon's application of western drilling techniques to the Orenburg field, testing 2,343 barrels per day, a four-fold rise on those wells using less advanced techniques.

"We anticipate that production from our nine new horizontal wells will come on line during the second half of 1997, giving us 25 horizontal and 11 vertical wells in production by the year end," Wieczorek added.
